lines.text: Years of judgment, written down nowhere. A recording shows what the expert did, never why.
Hi, I'm Clipa. I watch an expert work, ask why at the pauses, and coach the next person.
Three stages on one rail: show, reflect, pass it on.
Clipa, the teal paperclip, guides each one.
Step one, show: the expert works through the task in the demo workspace.
Clipa stays quiet while the expert types.
The typing stops. Clipa waits for a natural pause.
What determines whether you put customer 07's delivery address and time window in the email text or leave them in the attachment?
The image can stay as an extra; what matters is that the address and the delivery time are written in the email text.
Step two, reflect: a Work Map of steps, judgment calls and guardrails.
Why must the address and delivery time appear in the email text when the attached image contains them?
Because customer 07 asked us to send the delivery address and time as text in the email. Only for them; an extra image is fine.
Teach-back: Clipa reads back her understanding.
One correction: it is the delivery time window, not only the date.
Clarified that the email must include the delivery time window, not only the date. Everything else remains as recorded.
Confirmed by the expert, not written afterwards.
Step three, pass it on: a new hire, a new case for customer 07.
The draft only says: see the attached delivery summary.
The new hire moves to Send. Clipa checks the expert's confirmed rules.
The expert would stop here before sending and ask: why do you think this draft is ready to send?
She only warns, never clicks for you.
The new hire adds the address and time as text.
For customer 03, the same draft gets no warning. The rule is only for customer 07.
Off the record stops screen and voice at once.
It does not recall what was sent.
Clipa learns how your best people decide, teaches the next person, then your agents.
